m3-t1.question: What does the Agile Manifesto imply about documentation?
options: Documentation is the only measure of progress
Every document must be approved daily
It has value but working outcomes are valued more
m3-t1.explanation: The Manifesto values the items on the right, while valuing those on the left more.

m3-t1.question: Which condition particularly supports adaptive delivery?
options: All work is legally fixed and fully known
Uncertain user needs with access to feedback
m3-t1.explanation: Adaptive delivery uses learning to shape the solution.

m3-t1.question: What is a reasonable hybrid in the pilot?
options: Fixed approval gates with iterative workflow testing
m3-t1.explanation: Different parts of the work can require different control approaches.

m3-t1.question: What does seven of eight successful users establish?
options: A reason to omit further testing
A limited pilot observation to investigate
Proof that every user prefers the flow
m3-t1.explanation: A small pilot informs learning but does not establish broad certainty.

m3-t1.question: Which behaviour demonstrates useful adaptation?
options: Reorder work after reviewing evidence against the goal
m3-t1.explanation: Adaptation should be evidence-led and goal-oriented.

m3-t2.question: Who is accountable for effective Product Backlog management?
m3-t2.explanation: The Product Owner retains accountability even when work is delegated.

m3-t2.question: What is the Daily Scrum primarily for?
options: Developers inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan
m3-t2.explanation: It is a 15-minute event for Developers, not a reporting ceremony for managers.

m3-t2.question: Which commitment is associated with the Increment?
m3-t2.explanation: The Definition of Done describes the quality state required of the Increment.

m3-t2.question: How does Scrum describe backlog refinement?
options: The same event as Sprint Review
m3-t2.explanation: Refinement is ongoing work, not a named formal event.

m3-t2.question: An item fails the Definition of Done. How is it treated?
options: It counts if the card is moved
It counts if most effort is spent
It becomes Done at the Review automatically
It is not part of the Increment
m3-t2.explanation: Completion must be transparent and satisfy the shared quality standard.

m3-t3.question: Which is an end-to-end valuable slice?
options: A student can book one available slot safely
Write a list of all planned screens
m3-t3.explanation: A vertical slice supports a usable outcome, not only a technical layer.

m3-t3.question: What distinguishes acceptance criteria from the Definition of Done?
options: Done is only a delivery date
Criteria are item-specific; Done is a shared quality standard
m3-t3.explanation: Both matter, but at different scopes.

m3-t3.question: What is capacity for 28 available person-days at five focused hours per day?
What is an inappropriate use of velocity?
options: Inspecting its own historical trend carefully
m3-t3.explanation: Point scales and contexts differ across teams.

m3-t3.question: Who is accountable for ordering the Product Backlog?
m3-t3.explanation: Ordering is part of effective Product Backlog management.

questions.question: A team uses a daily meeting to receive assigned tasks from the sponsor. Which Scrum correction is most appropriate?
options: Rename the sponsor Scrum Master and keep the control pattern
Require customers to assign each task
Let Developers inspect progress and adapt their plan toward the Sprint Goal
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is not a sponsor task-dispatch meeting.

questions.question: Mid-Sprint learning makes an optional feature unnecessary. What can the team do while protecting the Sprint Goal?
options: Renegotiate scope with the Product Owner
Change the Sprint Goal casually every day
Mark the feature Done without work
Ban all discussion until the next month
questions.explanation: Scope can be clarified and renegotiated as learning occurs.

questions.question: A completed screen fails the shared security checks in Done. How should it appear in the Increment?
options: It counts after a status colour change
It must not count as Done
It counts because coding is complete
It counts if the sponsor likes it
questions.explanation: The Increment must meet the Definition of Done.

questions.question: Two teams have velocities 20 and 40 using different point scales. What conclusion is valid?
options: The first team should double every estimate
The numbers alone do not rank their productivity
The second team is exactly twice as productive
questions.explanation: Point scales and work contexts are not comparable productivity units.

questions.question: A fixed regulatory approval and uncertain user workflow coexist. Which approach is defensible?
options: Remove approvals in the name of Agile
Use ceremonies as proof of compliance
Retain mandatory gates and iterate the uncertain workflow
questions.explanation: Hybrid control can respect fixed constraints while enabling learning.

questions.question: Three people each have eight available days at four focused hours daily; support consumes twelve hours total. What capacity remains?
questions.explanation: 3×8×4 − 12 = 84 hours; this is not a point conversion.

questions.question: A backlog item says “build all database tables” but delivers no inspectable user outcome. What refinement helps?
options: Find a thin end-to-end booking slice and its acceptance examples
Rename the item an epic and stop
questions.explanation: A vertical slice enables meaningful feedback.

questions.question: A team postpones all feedback until the Sprint Review and claims release is prohibited earlier. What is accurate?
options: Every Review must approve a contract
Usable Done Increments may be released before the Review
Scrum requires one release only at project end
questions.explanation: The Review is not a mandatory release gate.

questions.question: Stakeholders ask the Scrum Master to order the Product Backlog instead of the Product Owner. What should be clarified?
options: The Scrum Master always owns ordering
The Product Owner retains backlog-management accountability
questions.explanation: Collaboration does not erase the Product Owner accountability.

questions.question: A pilot has favourable feedback from six volunteers. What should an adaptive plan do next?
options: Use the evidence with limitations and test remaining uncertainties
Replace the goal with every suggestion
questions.explanation: Empiricism requires honest interpretation and further learning.
